X.note: Weathered plaster, exposed brick, rubble, barrels and warm lit doorways give a lived-in, besieged feel, and the lighting has depth. The soldiers are stiff, mannequin-like 3D figures with identical poses, and they clump in the centre. One rubble-textured figure and some figures blend into the debris. The Union flag and the ship in the distance are tiny. The planar shutters are fine, but the bare window openings look slightly modern.

Y.note: Same scene, but the walls are clean, smooth, blue-grey slabs with no wear, no siege damage and almost no clutter. The cobbles are a uniform noisy texture, and the neat pale kerb makes it look like a modern CG street or a game level. The identical toy-like soldiers look worse against the sterile backdrop. The cool, flat lighting has little warmth or drama. Nothing here shows a town under bombardment.

why: X's weathered, damaged walls, rubble and warm light make a believable besieged street, while Y is a sterile, untextured game-level look with the same toy-like soldiers.
top_fix_for_weaker: Add heavy wall weathering (cracked plaster, exposed stone, shell damage), replace the uniform cobbles with irregular rubble and dirt, remove the tidy modern-looking kerb, and vary the soldiers' poses and spacing so they stop reading as mannequins.
anachronisms_seen: Union flag appears to be a post-1801 design (it has the red St Patrick's saltire); in 1782 it would have been the King's Colours with only the crosses of St George and St Andrew
Very clean, uniform, modern-looking kerb and wall finish in Y
Identical stiff soldier models in both frames, with inconsistent uniform details such as blue coats and cross-belts
